newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hog epidemic spreading rapidly - council.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hog epidemic spreading rapidly - council.

text.p: Officials said Taiwan's fast-moving hog foot and mouth epidemic had spread to 716 pig breeding centres as of late on Wednesday -- double the number reported on Monday.

Experts backed by soldiers continued a mass slaughter of hogs plagued by the highly contagious disease, with agriculture officials reporting that over 666,000 diseased and healthy pigs at affected farms would have to be destroyed.
As of Monday, the total was less than 400,00 pigs at 357 farms, according to statistics released by the cabinet's Council of Agriculture.
"We will keep on slaughtering all pigs at infected breeding farms," council secretary-general Lee Jen-chyuan said.
Industry sources quoted by the ruling Nationalist Party on Wednesday estimated that about 15 percent of Taiwan's 11 million swine -- or 1.6 million animals -- would be affected directly.
The farm council banned all pork exports after confirming the outbreak on March 20, when the virus had been found in just nine of the island's 25,000 hog breeding farms.

Across the island, masked soldiers in plastic suits have wielded electric prods to stun pigs, then used huge earth movers to dump them into incinerators or giant pits -- often with the pigs still gasping for air.
